data.name: Camillia
data.gender_notes: Camillia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Gentle youth, attendant on the sick
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Italian name Camillo, which comes from the Latin Camillus. Camillus is believed to have been named after the Roman god Camulus, who was the god of gardens and fertility. In Christian tradition, the name Camillia has a connection to Saint Camillus de Lellis, a nurse and religious order founder. He is the patron saint of hospitals, nurses, and the sick.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a gentle and compassionate girl, one who cares for those in need.
data.etymology: Camillia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle youth, attendant on the sick.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Camillia total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Καμιλλία
in_greek.meaning: Καμιλλία νόημα Καμιλλία για χριστιανική κοπέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καμιλλία προέρχεται από τη λατινική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'νεαρή κοπέλα' ή 'κοπέλα'. This name also represents the spiritual journey of carrying one's own crosses with faith and perseverance.

historical_references.reference: Camillus de Lellis was a soldier and a priest who founded the Order of Minims in the late 16th century. He was born in Italy, probably around 1550, and took the name Camillus after St. Camillus of Lepara, the patron saint of the sick and the wounded. The name Camillus is derived from the Latin word 'camillus' meaning 'helper', reflecting the saint's role as an attendant to the sick and the suffering.
historical_references.context: Italy; Founding of the Order of Minims

historical_references.reference: The name Camillia is also a rare given name for females, and it comes from the Latin word 'camellia', which is the name of the camellia flower. The camellia is believed to have originated in China and was introduced to Europe in the 16th century. The name Camillia may have been given to girls born during this time period in honor of the beautiful and fragrant camellia flower.
